title: Antimicrobial Mechanisms and Major Toxicities Compared
subject: Drug of Choice
preview: Beta-lactams inhibit bacterial cell-wall synthesis; macrolides act at the 50S ribosomal subunit; aminoglycosides act at 30S.
quickRevision: Beta-lactams inhibit bacterial cell-wall synthesis; macrolides act at the 50S ribosomal subunit; aminoglycosides act at 30S.
Aminoglycosides are associated with nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity; drug and renal monitoring can matter.
Antibiotic choice depends on infection site, severity, allergies and antimicrobial resistance patterns.

sections.title: Essential distinctions
points: Beta-lactams inhibit bacterial cell-wall synthesis; macrolides act at the 50S ribosomal subunit; aminoglycosides act at 30S.
Mechanism and spectrum must be considered alongside local susceptibility and patient-specific factors.
